Every Windows guard in internal/doctor is currently verified by construction — a sandboxGOOS override, a build tag, or a citation of Go's own Windows source. None is verified by observation. That is the gap.

tool_input.message:
PR went CLEAN and I attempted the merge; GitHub refused because Copilot filed one more thread seconds after my zero-thread check. This is the last one — everything else is green and resolved.

**`internal/doctor/procgroup_windows.go:12-14` — the comment overclaims, same defect class as the `procgroup_unix.go` one you already fixed.** It says `hookInvocationObserved` "returns via errSandboxUnsupportedPlatform before ever constructing a command on any GOOS reaching this file". The actual guard at `sandbox.go:113` is `sandboxGOOS == "windows"` only. The file is now tagged `!unix`, so it also compiles for plan9 and js/wasm, where that sentence is simply false — execution would proceed with process-group cleanup silently a no-op.

One fact Copilot did not have, which you should verify yourself and then state: `internal/doctor` does not build on plan9 today at all. `GOOS=plan9 go build ./internal/doctor/` fails because `internal/enable` → `internal/resolve` → `internal/process` carries `//go:build linux || darwin || windows`. So no non-Windows GOOS actually reaches that file right now. The claim is vacuously true in practice and wrong about the mechanism — which is exactly the kind of comment that becomes an outright lie the moment the transitive constraint changes, with nothing to catch it.

**Preferred fix — structural, not another corrected sentence.** Replace the string comparison with a build-tagged boolean declared in the same pair of files that already encode the platform split: something like `sandboxSupported = true` in `procgroup_unix.go` and `false` in `procgroup_windows.go`, with `hookInvocationObserved` gating on that. Then the guard and the build tag cannot drift apart, because they are the same fact declared once. That is the same lesson as the containment self-test earlier in this branch: assert the property rather than enumerate the cases you remembered.

Keep `sandboxGOOS` if the tests still need it to drive the Windows arm — I do not want the platform-split tests you just added to lose their seam. If the boolean makes `sandboxGOOS` redundant, say so and remove it; if both are needed, make the relationship explicit in a comment so nobody later "simplifies" one away.

Then correct the comment to state only what is true, and note the transitive-constraint fact so the next reader knows why plan9 is currently unreachable rather than assuming it is handled.

If you think the structural change is riskier than it is worth this late and a corrected comment is the better call, say so with reasoning — you have been right against me twice this round and I would rather hear the argument than get silent compliance.

Gates unchanged: `make check` green with race, both counts, five targets exit 0, plus `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go vet ./internal/doctor/`. Do not push — report and I push, then I merge.
